t a new
integration reads — and they are removed at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the
rename and so have no\ndeprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm`

emit both and accept either — never both in
one request — until general availability.

### Vocabulary

A name can move behin
d an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one field with\none string in it, and a client switching on `\"scenario\"` has no seco

nd name to
fall back to. So the values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `parentRef.ki
nd` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` |
`studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |\n| trace-destinati

on `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any other value is a
`400
`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vocabulary-1 request may use o
nly the legacy one, because\na boundary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one two\nimplementations can disagree abou

t. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-ev
al-vocabulary`, which is\neval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so rea
d\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are\ntwo blocks — before sending either. With the S

DK:
`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or
`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink res
ource types are the exception that proves the rule: `study` and\n`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `j
ourney_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION rather than the header — a
renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`\nlists b

oth.

### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted browser availability depends on the account and deployment. T
he browser workspace must be enabled to open the live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-sessions/messages` accepts an optiona
l `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it on every turn that should browse. The initial grant and profile are fixed; the cur
rent host policy and pinned read-only mode can narrow the effective permissions. Responses and traces include the read-only `chatS

essionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs without inline image data.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| POST
| `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, optional `profileId`, and a s
table `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the session browser. |\n| POST | `/ch
at-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execute a browser command under the session policy with a stable `commandId`. |\n| POST
| `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Append a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/trace
` | Read command receipts and screenshot evidence. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/artifact` | Resolve a command s

creenshot URL. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/close` | Release the session desktop. |

Only the owning user can
drive an API session's browser. All inputs use the public `sessionId`; conversation and browser identifiers in responses are info
rmational. Capacity refusals before execution release the turn lease so the same idempotency key can be retried. An execution with

an unknown outcome must be inspected before attempting a new action.
